claims.claim: bootstrap-primary attests the imported, non-editable legacy installed distribution in an isolated interpreter and rejects an install that already contains migrate-primary.

The bootstrap accepts the exact TASK-197 migration intent, restricts the target to reviewed commit 83115b26df85a7ad6643f317833e18b18586bdbe, checks downstream control, pins and TASK identity, and writes the existing exact-target handoff marker.
The bootstrap delegates target continuation to migrate-primary, creates no separate RUN path, rejects completed or ambiguous handoffs, and fails closed on orphaned pre-handoff transport.

Focused tests cover legacy-install isolation, mismatched identities, unsafe control, re-entry, one target RUN invocation and bounded interruption state; the shared migration transport retains the existing Windows path-budget test.
Brain Portability documentation distinguishes the bounded legacy bootstrap from the reusable N-to-N+1 migration invariant and retains explicit reviewed BP-9 adoption as the next consumer.
